title: St. Paul Boulevard Fire District unveils revised plan for Irondequoit firehouse
text:

The St. Paul Boulevard Fire Department holds a final meeting on plans to construct a modern firehouse, Wednesday, May 20, 2026. Irondequoit, N.Y.
— The St. Paul Boulevard Fire District has introduced a new proposal on Wednesday evening to construct a modern firehouse. The fire district held its final public meeting to explain to residents the critical need for a new firehouse. The fire chief highlighted the aging infrastructure of the current firehouse, built in 1990, noting problems such as leaking roofs and persistent plumbing issues.
“We're just asking, we've helped so many out there we need your help now to keep our firefighters safe and build a building that's going to be here for the next 50 plus years,” said Chief Ken Stavalone. The new facility would feature separate accommodations for men and women, along with advanced shower systems designed to meet cancer-reduction standards for firefighters.
The estimated project cost is $22 million, which would translate to approximately $62 per year in additional taxes for the average household.
“I don't think your plan is likely to be approved because it's too expensive,” said Joe Cassarino of Irondequoit. “Every person in this room has replaced an HVAC system. We don’t get to tear down our house because the roof leaks or the furnace breaks. We have to fix it.
We have great people in Monroe County that can bring this building back to where it needs to be. ” The chief says the department is also actively pursuing grant funding opportunities to offset the cost to taxpayers.
